conceptBreakdown.content: Proposed by Carl Woese, Otto Kandler, and Mark Wheelis (1990), the Three-Domain Model elevated the highest level of biological classification above the Kingdom level. It replaced the traditional Five-Kingdom system (Whittaker, 1969) by demonstrating that prokaryotes do not constitute a single monophyletic kingdom (Monera), but rather two distinct evolutionary domains: Bacteria and Archaea.

conceptBreakdown.heading: 4.1 The Molecular Clock: 16S / 18S rRNA Marker
conceptBreakdown.title: 4.1 The Molecular Clock: 16S / 18S rRNA Marker
conceptBreakdown.content:
Woese selected the small subunit ribosomal RNA (SSU rRNA) gene—specifically 16S rRNA in prokaryotes and 18S rRNA in eukaryotes—as the ultimate evolutionary chronometer based on the following structural criteria:

• Universal Distribution: Present in every cellular organism as a core component of translation machinery.

• Functional Constancy: Performs identical functional roles in protein synthesis across all life; thus, mutations are strictly filtered by natural selection.

• Conserved and Variable Regions: Contains highly conserved nucleotide regions (allowing universal PCR primer alignment) flanked by hypervariable regions that accumulate neutral mutations over evolutionary time scales (acting as a molecular clock).

conceptBreakdown.heading: 4.2 Comprehensive Comparative Analysis of the Three Domains
conceptBreakdown.title: 4.2 Comprehensive Comparative Analysis of the Three Domains
conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
MEMBRANE LIPID BIOCHEMISTRY
                       
        BACTERIA / EUKARYA                           ARCHAEA
        
     D-Glycerol-3-Phosphate                   L-Glycerol-1-Phosphate
            │                                        │
      [Ester Linkage]                          [Ether Linkage]
            │                                        │
     O=C─O─CH₂                                  O─CH₂
       │                                         │
     Unbranched Fatty Acid                    Branched Isoprenoid
       (Straight Chain)                        (Phytanyl Chain)
conceptBreakdown.content:
| Feature | Domain BACTERIA | Domain ARCHAEA | Domain EUKARYA |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Cellular Organization** | Prokaryotic (no membrane-enclosed nucleus or organelles) | Prokaryotic (no membrane-enclosed nucleus or organelles) | Eukaryotic (enclosed nucleus and membrane-bound organelles) |
| **Cell Wall Structure** | Present; composed of **Peptidoglycan** (Murein with $\beta$-1,4-linked NAG and NAM) | Lacks peptidoglycan; contains **Pseudopeptidoglycan** ($\beta$-1,3-linked NAG and NAT), S-layers, or complex polysaccharides | Present in plants/algae (cellulose, pectin) and fungi (chitin); absent in animals |
| **Membrane Lipid Architecture** | **Ester-linked**, unbranched fatty acid chains bound to D-glycerol-3-phosphate | **Ether-linked**, branched **isoprenoid** (phytanyl) chains bound to L-glycerol-1-phosphate | **Ester-linked**, unbranched fatty acid chains bound to D-glycerol-3-phosphate |
| **Membrane Bilayer vs. Monolayer** | Exclusively lipid bilayer | Can form **lipid monolayers** (biphytanyl tetraethers) conferring thermal stability in hyperthermophiles | Lipid bilayer containing sterols (cholesterol, ergosterol, phytosterols) |
| **First Amino Acid in Translation** | Formylmethionine (fMet) | Methionine (Met) | Methionine (Met) |
| **RNA Polymerase Enzymes** | Single simple RNA Polymerase (4 core subunits: $\alpha_2 \beta \beta^\prime \omega$) | Single complex RNA Polymerase (8–12 subunits; structurally homologous to Eukaryotic RNAP II) | Three complex RNA Polymerases (RNAP I, II, III; 12–14 subunits each) |
| **Introns in Genes** | Extremely rare (present only in tRNA/rRNA in special lineages) | Present in some structural and tRNA/rRNA genes | Ubiquitous in protein-coding nuclear genes |
| **Histone Proteins** | Absent; DNA condensed by HU and H-NS nucleoid proteins | Present in most lineages (form tetramer nucleosome-like structures) | Present (octameric histone complexes: H2A, H2B, H3, H4 + H1) |
| **Ribosomal Subunit Profile** | **70S** (30S subunit [16S rRNA] + 50S subunit [5S & 23S rRNA]) | **70S** (30S subunit [16S rRNA] + 50S subunit [5S & 23S rRNA]); structural shape closer to Eukarya | **80S** cytoplasmic (40S subunit [18S rRNA] + 60S subunit [5S, 5.8S, 28S rRNA]); 70S in organelles |
| **Sensitivity to Antibiotics** | Inhibited by Streptomycin, Chloramphenicol, Ampicillin | Insensitive to Streptomycin, Chloramphenicol, and Ampicillin | Insensitive to prokaryotic translation inhibitors |
| **Sensitivity to Diphtheria Toxin** | Insensitive | Sensitive (ADP-ribosylation of elongation factor EF-2) | Sensitive (ADP-ribosylation of elongation factor EF-2) |

conceptBreakdown.heading: 4.3 Key Evolutionary Insights for NEST
conceptBreakdown.title: 4.3 Key Evolutionary Insights for NEST
conceptBreakdown.content:
• Prokaryote is a Grade, Not a Clade: The term 'prokaryote' describes a structural grade (absence of a membrane-enclosed nucleus), not a monophyletic taxon.

• Sister Taxa Relationship: Molecular analysis of transcription, translation, and replication machinery shows that Archaea and Eukarya are sister domains, sharing a more recent common ancestor with each other than either does with Bacteria.

quickRevision: Woese 3 domains = Bacteria, Archaea, Eukarya based on 16S/18S rRNA.
Archaea: Pseudopeptidoglycan (β-1,3), Ether-linked isoprenoid lipids (tetraether monolayers), Met, Eukaryotic-like RNAP.
Archaea and Eukarya are sister domains; Prokaryote is a grade, not a clade.
